html:
On 15 February 1989 the last Soviet troops left Afghanistan, crossing the Friendship Bridge over the Amu Darya to Termez, ending nearly ten years of the Soviet war in Afghanistan.

Mikhail Gorbachev had called the war a bleeding wound. Under the Geneva Accords of 1988 the Soviet army left in stages. About 15,000 Soviet soldiers had died, and estimates of Afghan dead run from about half a million to two million; millions more were refugees. The last commander, General Boris Gromov, walked across the bridge alone at the end.

The communist government of Mohammad Najibullah held on, with Soviet aid, until 1992, when the mujahideen took Kabul and the civil war began. The defeat weakened the Soviet army and state, which broke up in 1991.
sum: On 15 February 1989 the last Soviet troops left Afghanistan, crossing the Friendship Bridge over the Amu Darya to Termez, ending nearly ten years of the Soviet war in Afghanistan.
